inherited_methods.input: w_N(n)=log(N/n)/log N and sum_(n in E)w_N(n)>=1 for every bad support
inherited_methods.loss_step: replace each arithmetic bad support by the single scalar inequality sum_E w_N>=1 and then apply a generic cover relaxation
inherited_methods.lost_information: prime-incidence overlap among different circuits and a canonical choice of an integer vertex
inherited_methods.exact_loss: LP feasibility records total defect on an edge but forgets arithmetic overlap among edges and supplies no integral vertex choice
inherited_methods.consequence: a generic integrality loss of order log N converts N/log N only to O(N), not o(N)
inherited_methods.required_repair: an arithmetic rounding loss o(log N), or a direct o(N) transversal

inherited_methods.input: delete n<=N^(1-1/L), thereby eliminating relations whose larger shore has at most L elements
inherited_methods.loss_step: replace the sum of all edge defects by the maximum defect of one vertex
inherited_methods.lost_information: accumulation of arbitrarily many small vertex defects and the prime-incidence shape of their circuit
inherited_methods.exact_loss: it retains only the maximum individual defect and discards how arbitrarily many tiny defects sum to one
inherited_methods.consequence: balanced nonuniform 2-adic padding embeds support-minimal unbalanced circuits in every fixed power-thin tail
inherited_methods.required_repair: use prime-incidence or circuit overlap, not only w_N(n) or relation length

inherited_methods.input: sample vertices with probabilities proportional to w_N or take a finite union of global defect thresholds
inherited_methods.loss_step: control each edge separately and discard the joint arithmetic dependency graph before demanding simultaneous coverage
inherited_methods.lost_information: which failure events share valuation fibres and whether residual edges admit a globally chargeable repair
inherited_methods.exact_loss: each long tight circuit retains positive miss probability; threshold unions collapse to one pointwise cutoff, while the edge family has no proved usable dependency bound
inherited_methods.consequence: expectation and per-edge success do not yield a simultaneous transversal
inherited_methods.required_repair: dependent selection with an arithmetic witness map, resampling theorem with proved dependency control, or deterministic alteration charged globally

inherited_methods.input: remove a y-smooth core and use valuation balance in fibres p>y
inherited_methods.loss_step: assign or charge a multi-large-prime integer in one fibre while forgetting its incidences in every other active prime fibre
inherited_methods.lost_information: cross-fibre congestion and the lower-prime residues carried by balanced top-fibre terms
inherited_methods.exact_loss: one integer can lie in several large-prime fibres, so a valuation equation balances incidences rather than term counts; naive endpoint charges can be repeated at many prime scales
inherited_methods.consequence: private-prime and uniform one-endpoint arguments do not bound total congestion
inherited_methods.required_repair: a canonical ownership/coarea rule with a proved o(log N) load, or a sharp obstruction to every rule in a frozen class

inherited_methods.input: round using rank of the prime-exponent matrix or maximum circuit size
inherited_methods.loss_step: compress the signed circuit family to one global rank or size statistic
inherited_methods.lost_information: local valuation support, circuit overlap, and the number of prime scales charging a fixed integer
inherited_methods.exact_loss: rank can be large on a single cheaply hit circuit and circuit size is unbounded; neither statistic measures overlap of deletion witnesses
inherited_methods.consequence: ordinary rank/size inequalities need not give o(N)
inherited_methods.required_repair: a weighted local rank, coarea, or fibre-depth invariant that pays each integer at few scales

inherited_methods.method: fixed-N exact ILP and dual inspection
inherited_methods.input: enumerate all bad supports and optimize at a bounded cutoff
inherited_methods.loss_step: discard the symbolic dependence on N after solving the finite incidence instance
inherited_methods.lost_information: uniform arithmetic structure and stabilization of witnesses across cutoffs
inherited_methods.exact_loss: the relation hypergraph and its dual witnesses change with N, and no finite motif-completeness theorem is available
inherited_methods.consequence: larger cutoffs cannot imply an asymptotic rounding theorem
inherited_methods.required_repair: extract and prove one symbolic all-parameter inequality or counterfamily

inherited_methods.input: admit integers having valuation one at exactly one prime from a selected set
inherited_methods.loss_step: force every admitted integer into a private diagonal prime fibre
inherited_methods.lost_information: the possibility of safely reusing several prime fibres per integer
inherited_methods.exact_loss: diagonal prime fibres give an exact cardinality certificate but the cylinder density is at most 1/e
inherited_methods.consequence: private diagonalization cannot approach density one
inherited_methods.required_repair: permit reused prime fibres while retaining triangular or bounded-load control

inherited_methods.input: choose finite transversals independently and concatenate or diagonalize them
inherited_methods.loss_step: forget all multiplicative constraints between different cutoffs, blocks, or cylinders
inherited_methods.lost_information: cross-block relations, pointwise stabilization, and an actual density limit
inherited_methods.exact_loss: multiplicative relations cross blocks and finite decisions need not stabilize
inherited_methods.consequence: finite density-one, even if proved, does not automatically give one natural-density set
inherited_methods.required_repair: a hereditary/profinite rule with cross-cylinder isolation and an actual density limit

required_new_information: A vertex ownership or alteration rule exploiting the full prime-incidence pattern of each minimal {-1,0,1} circuit.
A proved global congestion bound o(log N) relative to the promoted log-defect mass.
A smooth-core recursion that accounts for integers having several large prime divisors without converting incidence balance into term balance illegally.
For the infinite target, stabilization of every fixed decision together with zero upper density of deletions and a cross-scale relation theorem.
For negative progress, an all-parameter circuit embedding or integrality-gap theorem against a precisely specified rounding class.

frozen_countermodel.name: balanced 2-adic padding of edge-prime circuits
frozen_countermodel.statement: For every positive sequence eta_K with K eta_K tending to infinity, every sufficiently large power N=2^K contains a support-minimal unequal-cardinality equal-product relation wholly in (N^(1-eta_K),N].
frozen_countermodel.effect: refutes every lower-power-tail threshold whose deletion cost is o(N), as well as finite nested repetitions of such thresholds
frozen_countermodel.does_not_refute: smooth-core deletion followed by full multi-prime ownership, or any rounding using more than pointwise defect
